title.en: What Would Your Gift Note Say?
title.zh: 礼物旁的小纸条：你会写什么？

description.en: Six small-note choices about a shared memory, a specific thank-you and a gentle wish. Find the voice your choices give a simple gift note.
description.zh: 六次小纸条选择，写一段共同记忆、一声具体感谢或一个轻轻祝愿，看看你会给简单礼物配上怎样的声音。

introduction.en: Imagine writing a note beside an ordinary gift, something handmade or a small thing you already have. Nothing needs to be bought for this quiz. Choose what you want the note to carry; the result does not measure love, generosity or relationship quality.
introduction.zh: 想象给普通礼物、手作或已有小物写张便条。做测试不需要购买东西。选你想让纸条带着什么；结果不衡量爱、慷慨或关系质量。

focus.en: Expressing attention through one shared memory, one concrete acknowledgment or one wish that leaves the recipient free.
focus.zh: 通过一段共同记忆、一项具体致谢，或不替对方规定的祝愿，表达关注。

prompt.en: The blank card has room for just two lines. You begin with…

label.en: A small moment the two of you still remember.
label.zh: 两人仍记得的一个小瞬间。

label.en: Something specific they did that you appreciated.
label.zh: 对方做过而你欣赏的一件具体事。

label.en: A simple wish for something they themselves want.
label.zh: 为对方自己想要的事送一句简单祝愿。

prompt.en: The gift is very ordinary. Your note makes it personal by…
prompt.zh: 礼物很普通，你用纸条让它有个人联系的方式是……

label.en: Linking it to a shared little story.
Naming why you thought they might enjoy it now.
label.zh: 说清为什么想到对方此刻也许会喜欢。

label.en: Saying what you are grateful for without assigning a debt.
label.zh: 说清感谢什么，不附回报债务。

prompt.en: You remove one sentence that feels too grand. You replace it with…
prompt.zh: 删去一句觉得太宏大的话，你换成……

label.en: A plain thank-you for one real action.
label.zh: 对一个真实行动的朴素感谢。

label.en: One detail from an ordinary day together.
label.zh: 共同普通一天里的一个细节。

label.en: A short hope that does not tell them how life should go.
label.zh: 一句不规定人生该怎样的短祝愿。

prompt.en: You do not know exactly what the recipient will do next. You…
prompt.zh: 不知道对方接下来具体怎样安排，你会……

label.en: Wish them room to choose their own next step.
label.zh: 祝愿对方有空间选择自己的下一步。

label.en: Stay with something already shared rather than predicting the future.
label.zh: 写已经共享的事，不预测未来。

label.en: Thank them for what they have already chosen to contribute.
label.zh: 感谢对方已经主动做过的贡献。

prompt.en: The note needs a closing line. You choose…
prompt.zh: 便条需要最后一句，你选……

label.en: I still smile when I remember that tiny moment.
label.zh: 想起那个小瞬间，我仍会笑。

label.en: Thank you for that particular kindness; no reply needed.
label.zh: 谢谢那一份具体善意，不用专门回复。

label.en: I hope you find a version of the next chapter you enjoy.
label.zh: 愿你找到自己喜欢的下一段版本。

prompt.en: What would you most like the reader to feel from this little card?
prompt.zh: 最希望读者从小卡里感到什么？

label.en: A simple act they chose was noticed.
label.zh: 自己主动做的一件小事被看见。

label.en: There is room for the future to be theirs.
label.zh: 未来有空间由自己决定。

label.en: One small part of our shared history still matters.
label.zh: 共同历史里的一小部分仍有意义。

summary.en: Your note keeps a little piece of time the two of you already share. A small detail can make an ordinary object feel connected without a grand declaration. This is the voice you chose for this card, not the only way you express care.
summary.zh: 你的纸条留下一小块两人已经共享的时间。一个小细节，就能让普通物件有联系，不必宏大宣言。这是本卡所选声音，不是你表达关心的唯一方式。

example.en: A handmade bookmark might carry a line about the rainy afternoon when you both kept rereading the same funny paragraph.
example.zh: 一枚手作书签，可以配一句：记得雨天下午，两人反复读同一段有趣文字。

strength.en: A specific memory can feel personal because it belongs to a recognizable moment rather than a phrase that could be sent unchanged to anyone.
strength.zh: 具体记忆有个人意味，因为它属于可辨认瞬间，不是一句可原封不动发给所有人的话。

tradeoff.en: The same event may mean different things to each person. Keeping the note modest leaves room for their version of the memory too.
tradeoff.zh: 同一件事对双方可能意义不同。便条写得适度，也给对方记忆版本留空间。

experiment.en: Write two plain lines about a harmless shared moment. Keep one concrete detail and leave out any claim about what the other person must remember or feel.
experiment.zh: 为一个无害共同瞬间写两句普通话。留一个具体细节，不替对方规定一定记得或感到什么。

summary.en: Your card names something the recipient actually did. The thanks can stand on its own rather than becoming a request for more of the same. This ending values a concrete acknowledgment without measuring either person’s generosity.
summary.zh: 你的卡片说出对方实际做过什么。感谢本身成立，不变成继续这样做的请求。结局珍惜具体致意，不衡量任何一方慷慨多少。

example.en: You might thank a friend for sending the map that made your small outing easier, instead of telling them they must always be the organized one.
example.zh: 你可能感谢朋友发来让小外出更方便的地图，不说对方以后必须一直当有条理的人。

strength.en: Naming the act makes appreciation understandable and lets the recipient know what reached you without assigning them a permanent helping role.
strength.zh: 说清行动让欣赏易懂，也让对方知道什么被接收，而不被分配永久帮忙角色。

tradeoff.en: A thank-you can become heavy if it carries expectations of a particular response. A brief note can leave the receiver free to accept it quietly.
tradeoff.zh: 若带着必须怎样回应的期待，感谢也会重。短便条可以让接收者安静收下。

experiment.en: Thank someone for one specific voluntary act and stop there. Leave out a request, a repayment promise or a prediction of what they will do next.
experiment.zh: 为一个具体自愿行动向人道谢，就停在那里。不附请求、偿还承诺或对之后行动的预测。

summary.en: Your note offers a wish without writing the recipient’s future for them. You can hope something goes well while leaving the form of that good outcome open. The portrait describes a small message, not your ability to predict what another person needs.
summary.zh: 你的便条送祝愿，不代写对方未来。可以希望事情顺利，也让怎样算好结果保持开放。画像描述小信息，不证明你能预测别人需要什么。

example.en: For a friend starting a hobby, you might wish them enjoyable time with it rather than promising that it will become their new passion.
example.zh: 朋友开始一项爱好，你可能祝有愉快相处时间，不许诺它会成为对方新的热爱。

strength.en: An open wish can feel supportive without making a particular achievement or emotional response a condition of receiving the gift.
strength.zh: 开放祝愿可以支持人，不把特定成就或情绪反应设成收下礼物的条件。

tradeoff.en: A very broad wish can sound distant. Linking it to something the person has actually said they want gives the note a more particular shape.
tradeoff.zh: 祝愿太宽也会显远。连到对方实际表达过想要的东西，便条会更具体。

experiment.en: Write one short wish tied to a preference the person has expressed. Keep their freedom to change that preference visible in the wording.
experiment.zh: 为对方说过的一个偏好写短祝愿，也在措辞里保留以后改变偏好的自由。
